value.actual_behavior:
Neither holds. The paper/live control is named three different ways across
four order endpoints and the defaults diverge: omitting it on an event-card
trade or a bot clone inherits user.simulation_mode, while omitting `mode` on
an exchange order is documented as "live". The CLOB order schema has no such
field at all. And user.simulation_mode, the setting two of those resolve
against, appears three times in openapi-public.json — every occurrence prose
inside a request body. No documented response returns it and llms.txt does not
mention it.
value.description:
We are not reporting that the modes are wired wrongly. Each endpoint probably
does exactly what its own description says. The defect is that an autonomous
caller cannot act on them safely, and /build is an invitation to autonomous
callers specifically.
The concrete failure: an agent sets itself to paper, writes one helper that
omits the optional flag because omitting it worked against the event-card
endpoint, and then places a REAL order the first time that helper is pointed
at the exchange. Nothing in the response to any prior call would have warned
it, because the setting it thought it was inheriting is not published anywhere
it can read.
We got this wrong ourselves today, which is why we think it is worth your
time. Reading an unauthenticated fetch of /aci-challenge, we saw "PAPER
TRADING MODE" and concluded our own account was in paper. It is live, with
real USDC in it. The badge in the logged-in UI says so plainly — the API says
nothing at all, and we had no way to check without the browser.
Two changes would close it, and they are independent: publish the effective
mode on a read an agent already makes (portfolio/summary or /mcp/v1/agents/me
would both be natural), and make the four order endpoints agree on one field
name and one default. If you would rather not change the exchange default,
saying so in the field description — "unlike the event-card endpoints, this
does not inherit simulation_mode" — would remove most of the risk on its own.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-the_setting_that_decides_whether_real_money_moves_is_readable] user.simulation_mode decides whether an order spends real USDC when the per-trade flag is omitted, and no documented response publishes it: all three occurrences in the schema are prose inside request bodies, so an agent cannot read the setting it is about to inherit
    left: []
    right: ['a response field naming the mode']
    sources: {'schema': '/openapi-public.json'}
    population: {'prose_mentions': 3, 'response_fields': 0}

  [CYM-every_order_endpoint_decides_the_book_the_same_way] the order endpoints name the paper/live control 4 different ways (None, is_paper, mode, paper) and disagree on what omitting it means (None, live); clob order offers no control at all
    left: ['clob order: None default=None', 'clone a bot: is_paper default=None', 'event-cards buy: paper default=None', 'event-cards sell: paper default=None', 'event-cards short: paper default=None', 'exchange order: mode default=live']
    right: ['one field, one default, on every order endpoint']
    sources: {'schema': '/openapi-public.json'}
    population: {'endpoints': 6, 'distinct_fields': 4, 'distinct_defaults': 2}

REPRODUCE:
  - GET https://cymetica.com/openapi-public.json
  - Read BuyRequest.paper — the description gives the resolution order: body.paper, then user.simulation_mode, then the platform-wide gate
  - Read CloneBotRequest.is_paper — "If None, inherits user's simulation_mode"
  - Read src__api__routes__exchange__PlaceOrderRequest.mode — "Trading mode: 'live' or 'paper'", default "live"
  - Read src__api__routes__clob__PlaceOrderRequest.properties — no paper or mode field exists
  - Search the whole document for a RESPONSE property matching simulation_mode -> none; all three occurrences are request-body prose

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/rest/test_paper_or_real.py::test_every_order_endpoint_decides_the_book_the_same_way
  tests/rest/test_paper_or_real.py::test_the_setting_that_decides_whether_real_money_moves_is_readable

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
